subject: Post-demo follow-up: what Redwood stores for prompts & outputs
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@healthflow.com>

Cc: security@healthflow.com
Date: 2029-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: quick follow on what gets stored

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great walkthrough. We had a couple of follow-ups from our security and engineering leads about data handling for interactive prompts. Could you confirm the following at a high level so we can map to our data classification?

1) Which parts of a user session are persisted by default (prompt inputs, model outputs, intermediate tokens, embedding vectors)?
2) What are the default retention windows for each stored artifact (logs, prompts, outputs, audit trails)?
3) In hosted mode, where is the data physically stored (region/US/EU)? Are there options to keep everything in our VPC or on Dedicated hardware?
4) Who at Redwood has access to raw prompt text and outputs (engineers, support, SRE)? Is access audited?

We attached a short spreadsheet of our data classification to help label items. Goal: determine if we need a Private deployment or if hosted defaults can meet our requirements.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick follow on what gets stored

Hi Elena — really helpful spreadsheet, thanks for sending. Below is a concise mapping based on hosted defaults and what we can change for Dedicated/Private deployments. I also attached a short one-pager.

Summary (hosted API default):
- Prompt inputs: persisted in encrypted request logs for billing/telemetry and debugging. Default retention = 14 days. Prompts are encrypted at rest; keys managed by Redwood for hosted tenants.
- Model outputs: not persisted permanently by default. Generated outputs are stored transiently for streaming and delivery; full output snapshots are retained for up to 24 hours for delivery retry and analytics and then removed unless the customer opts into session recording.
- Token-level streaming / KV cache: KV cache lives in GPU memory only during the session and is not written to disk or object storage. We do not persist KV caches across sessions in hosted mode.
- Embeddings / derived vectors: we persist embeddings only when a customer explicitly calls the embeddings API or enables vector indexing; retention follows the same 14-day default unless otherwise configured.
- Metadata / audit logs: request metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts, error codes) retained 90 days in hosted plans for debugging and rate-limiting analysis. Enterprise contracts can extend or shorten these windows.

Access and controls:
- Who can see raw prompt text: by default, Redwood engineers do not access raw customer prompts except under narrow, audited troubleshooting cases and with customer approval. Access is gated through our internal RBAC and recorded in audit logs.
- Admin options: Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments control encryption keys (KMS/HSM) and can request that raw text never leave their VPC.
- Regions: Hosted data is stored in the region you select at account creation (we offer us-west, us-east, and eu-west). Residents are pinned to that region unless cross-region routing/policy is enabled.

Retention options we recommend for HealthFlow during POC:
- Keep hosted defaults for short-term evaluation (14-day prompt logs, 24-hour outputs).
- If you need longer auditability for clinical workflows, recommend Dedicated with 90-day prompt retention and customer-managed keys.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will upload our SOC2 snapshot and a short redwood-prompt-storage-summary.pdf to the shared Drive (link below).
2) Schedule a 30-minute compliance deep-dive with your security team — can you share 2 windows next week?
3) If you prefer, we can spin up a short Dedicated evaluation for HealthFlow to demonstrate KMS controls and extended retention.

Thanks — looping in Dylan for a couple of technical clarifications below.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick technical clarification from infra side:
- KV cache: ephemeral in-GPU state only; we never serialize the KV cache to object storage in hosted mode. That means no persistent intermediate attentional state is kept across sessions.
- Streaming buffer: we temporarily buffer streamed tokens to guarantee delivery and resume; those buffers are rotated within ephemeral storage and scrubbed within 24 hours by default (longer only if session recording is enabled).
- Debug snapshots: when customers consent to share logs for debugging, we create timeboxed snapshots (explicitly requested, access controlled, and logged).

Attaching a small diagram that shows data transit for a typical hosted request.

- Dylan Brooks
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
